action_items.description: Add rule to dev SOUL.md: ROOT CAUSE FIRST — When a task title references 'original fix task reopened (fix didn't resolve root cause)', you MUST read the original fix before writing any code. Steps: (1) grep git log for the original task short ID from the title; (2) run 'git show <branch>:<changed-files>' to read what was changed; (3) identify WHY the fix didn't hold (symptom-level patch vs root cause?); (4) write your fix targeting the root cause, not the symptom. A fix that repeats the same approach as the previous fix will fail QC for the same reason and waste a full pipeline cycle.
action_items.reason: 3 of 5 dev failures this review are 'Cancelled: original fix task reopened (fix didn't resolve root cause)'. Dev agents restart work without reading the previous fix, producing the same surface patch. Each wasted cycle costs $2+ and a full pipeline slot.

action_items.description: Add rule to dev SOUL.md: GATE PRE-CHECK — At the start of any task whose title begins with 'Fix: Quality gate', immediately re-run the failing gate before touching code. Command: npm run <gate-name> (or the relevant check). If the gate now passes, write a completion report with notes='no-op: gate already resolved before agent started' and call reportSuccess() — do NOT make any code changes. Phantom gate-fix tasks that apply changes to an already-green gate leave the codebase in an inconsistent state.
action_items.reason: 1 of 5 dev failures was 'Auto-resolved: gate now passes'. The gate fixed itself before the agent started (from a concurrent task), but the agent was already spawned. Without a pre-check, the agent will apply a fix to a resolved problem.

action_items.description: Add rule to dev SOUL.md: GIT RETRY ON TIMEOUT — When any git network operation (git push, git fetch, git clone, git ls-remote, branch creation via remote) times out or returns a connection error, retry up to 3 times with 10-second sleep between attempts before marking the operation as failed. Do NOT fail the entire task on first network timeout. Use: for i in 1 2 3; do git <operation> && break || sleep 10; done. Log each retry attempt. Only fail the task if all 3 retries fail.
action_items.reason: 1 of 5 dev failures was 'branch-creation-failed: timeout exceeded when trying to connect'. Transient network timeouts during git operations should not abort an entire task — they are recoverable with a simple retry.

action_items.description: Add rule to qc SOUL.md: DEDUP PR CHECK — At task start, before checking out any branch, run: SELECT id, status FROM tasks WHERE agent_id='qc' AND pr_number=<this_pr_number> AND status IN ('done','in_progress','ready') AND id != '<this_task_id>'. If a matching row exists, log the duplicate task ID and call reportSuccess() with notes='no-op: QC already completed or in-progress for PR #<number>'. Do NOT duplicate a QC review that another QC task already completed.
action_items.reason: 3 of 4 QC 'failures' this week were duplicate tasks cancelled with 'Archived: duplicate — UC already has successful task for this agent'. The cascade cancellations (parent dev failed) are correct behavior, but duplicate QC spawns for the same PR waste spawn slots and budget.

action_items.description: Genome spawn-consumer creates duplicate QC tasks for the same PR number. Add a dedup check in the QC task creation path (workflow-engine.js createTask or chainTask for agent_id='qc'): before inserting, query SELECT id FROM tasks WHERE agent_id='qc' AND pr_number=<pr_number> AND status NOT IN ('cancelled','failed'). If a row exists, skip creation and log 'QC task already exists for PR #<pr_number>'. This prevents the 3-duplicate pattern seen this week.
action_items.reason: 3 QC tasks were cancelled as duplicates for PRs already reviewed. The dedup check in createTask() doesn't catch this because it deduplicates by title, not by (agent_id, pr_number) — and QC task titles include the PR number which may differ from the dedup_key used.
